principle: Tarawa lessons improve US preparation and local response, but added vehicles, landing craft, fire-support missions and engineering teams share finite lagoon, beach-exit, radio, observation and escort capacity.
observed_problem: Suppressed Japanese positions reman after naval fire lifts.
Lagoon-side direct fire is better oriented than the historical surprise case.
More LVT/LST/LCI reserve causes local wave and exit queues if launched without metering.
Smoke/dust and repeated direct-fire calls compete for observation and safe-fire sectors.
US_adaptation_same_day: Hold or meter later waves rather than filling blocked beach exits.
Use destroyers/LVT(A)/artillery for rapid re-suppression of remanned firing points.
Keep tanks behind engineer-cleared lanes instead of forcing armor through crater/debris bottlenecks.
Shift close-support sorties from broad area attack toward observed strongpoints and mortar/communication nodes.
Do not interpret one suppression report as permanent destruction.
net: US material superiority converts to effective combat power with short local delays rather than unlimited simultaneity. This caps Japanese gains from better preparation while preserving a visibly higher D-Day casualty/friction level than the superseded v003 line.
